description: Cisco Network Convergence System 5001, a one-rack-unit router with forty 1/10G SFP+ ports and four 100G QSFP28 ports. The ports, the console and the management jack are on the port (front) side; two power supplies, two fan modules and a USB port are on the other. Ships port-side intake or port-side exhaust and with AC or DC supplies, four builds of one front panel. The guide says nothing about end-of-sale; the status is unknown.

gaps.wanted: Whether the NCS 5001 is on sale. The one held document is silent; the intake grid marks every NCS model unknown. An end-of-sale notice or the product page would settle it.

A flat front and rear elevation, or a photograph taken square on. The guide's Figures 1 and 2 are greyscale three-quarter views, so every position is estimated and no printed numeral or legend can be read.
The legends printed beside the ports, lamps and jacks. None is resolved in the held figures, so none is drawn, and the model name is not drawn either because nothing shows it as printed.
Which 24 of the 40 SFP+ cages are the purple DWDM and ZR capable ones. The guide gives the counts and the colour and no position.

What the two round features beside the USB port on the fan side are, and their size. Figure 1 shows them and the text names only the USB interface; "An ESD socket is provided on the chassis" gives no position, so they are drawn as unnamed discs and not as ESD sockets.

The rack-mount kit as a kit contract: part numbers, the dimensions of the bracket, guide and slider rail, and the rack depth range. The guide gives a parts list (Table 8; accessory kit NCS-5001-ACSR in Appendix A) whose counts disagree, and a rack requirement of 23.5 to 34.0 in between the outside faces of the front and rear rails.

The management jack's rate. Searched the guide for "10/100", "1000", "Gigabit" and "speed" beside the management interface: it names the interface and the console's RS-232 and gives no rate for the jack.
The fan module's power draw, and the chassis' own draw. Appendix C gives supply ratings only.

The air filters, which the guide draws but does not size or number. Port-side intake takes a three-piece filter on the port-side faceplate (Figure 22); port-side exhaust takes clip-on filters on the supply and fan fronts (Figure 23). No part number, size or position is held for either.
A drawing of the rest of the lid, the underside and the side walls. The guide shows them in three-quarter view only, with six bracket holes on a side wall and a grounding label on the fan side.

attrs.redundancy-note: guide Chapter 1, Fan Modules: "slots for two 1+1 redundant fan modules", hot-swappable; "The system can work with a single fan failure. More than one fan failure leads to system shutdown."

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band ports - an RJ-45 console on the port side with an RJ-45 management jack, and a USB port on the fan side. Two media and a USB, one purpose: reaching the router when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: guide Chapter 1, Features: "Two 1+1 redundant, hot-swappable power supplies", and "A minimum of one power supply is required for normal operation".

name: ncs-5001

airflow.note: Chapter 2, Airflow Direction: front-to-back is "port side intake" and back-to-front is "port side exhaust", set by the type of fan modules and power supplies, and "it is not possible to mix airflow directions". The two builds are configurations. THE GUIDE GIVES NO COLOUR FOR EITHER DIRECTION in text or in its greyscale figures (it says only that a replacement has "the same coloring as the other fan and power supply modules in the same chassis"), so no handle colour is set per configuration. Figure 21, a colour drawing of a DC supply, shows a green latch; it does not say which airflow that is.

arrangement.note: READ OFF FIGURE 2 AND THE RACK-MOUNTING FIGURES 7 AND 8, which show the same face from the same angle: two rows of cages, a gap in each row that splits it into two groups of equal length, a two-by-two block of larger cages at the right end, and a cluster of lamps and two stacked jacks at the left. Twenty cages a row is the guide's 40 over two rows; ten a group is the cage count in each group of Figure 2, and the 2.5 mm gutter is a guess. The row pitch is the registry's 15.0 mm stack figure and the two rows are centred on the 43.7 mm face. The QSFP28 block takes the 24.4 mm column step and 16.8 mm row step the library uses elsewhere.

colour.note: The face is a light grey with dark printing in the guide's greyscale figures; #c9cccf is chosen by eye, not sampled.

configuration-names.note: THE GUIDE GIVES NO CHASSIS PART NUMBER AND NO CODE FOR ANY BUILD. Its only orderable codes for this router are the supplies and fan modules (Tables 2 and 3) and the accessory kit NCS-5001-ACSR, and it says "power supply options need to be configured with the base chassis". The four configurations are therefore one `kind: base` build (AC, port-side intake) and three `kind: example` builds, with no `part-numbers`: each says which supplies and fan modules it seats, and none is an orderable SKU.

console-and-management.note: Two RJ-45 jacks stacked at the left of the port side, the console over the management jack, as the library draws them on other Cisco boxes. Figure 2 shows a column of two stacked jacks there beside a small lamp cluster; the guide's text names a console and a management interface and gives no more.

dimensions.note: Appendix C, Table 11, p.41: "1.72 x 17.42 x 19.3 in. (4.37 cm x 44.3 cm x 49.0 cm)". The inch figures are carried, converted to 43.7 x 442.5 x 490.2 mm; the centimetre figures round to 44.3 and 49.0 and are within 0.6 mm of the same numbers. The guide's Cabinet and Rack Installation appendix states a minimum of one rack unit. Whether the width includes the rack-mount brackets is not stated; the brackets are a separate kit (Table 8) and are not drawn.

ears-and-kits.note: The `flush` position is the one Figures 7 and 8 draw: the front bracket bolts to the side of the chassis with its flange level with the port-side face. The guide says "any four of the holes in the front rack-mount bracket" meet "four of the six screw holes" in the chassis, so other positions exist, and none is measured; they are not written. NO KIT IS MODELLED: Table 8 lists the rack-mount kit as four brackets, sixteen M4 screws, four rack-mount guides and two slider rails, and Appendix A lists accessory kit NCS-5001-ACSR with two of each bracket and guide, so the guide disagrees with itself on the counts; no document held gives a bracket's, a guide's or a slider's dimensions or the kit's depth range. The library's kit contracts (`cisco/69-2037`, `cisco/n9k-c9500-rmk`) are for other boxes and none fits this one. See the gaps.

gate-1.note: FAILED AND SAID SO. Figure 2 (front) and Figure 1 (rear) are not orthographic: the near end of each face is drawn larger than the far end, so no px/mm can be derived from them and the aspect cannot be compared with Table 11's 442.5 by 43.7 mm. Only fractions of the face width were taken, along the near edge, and a repeated feature of known size is the ruler: ten SFP cages at 14.25 mm abut for 142.5 mm, and each group of ten reads about a third of the cage field in Figure 2. Every x and y on both faces is therefore estimated; the counts are the guide's.

intake-mesh.note: Figure 2 (printed page 2, front view) shows a black perforated strip along the port-side edge, as long as the cage field and beyond it, with the cages in the face below it. IT IS ON THE LID, NOT ON THE FACE: the strip lies in the top surface at the front edge, so it is drawn in the top view and the front elevation stays plain. From about 4% to 97% of the near edge (412.5 mm of 442.5) and, by the figure's foreshortening, about a ninth of the lid depth (54.0 mm), a two-millimetre lip of lid beyond it. Fractions of a perspective drawing, so every number is an estimate. The guide's maintenance text says "a replaceable air filter is located on the front of the chassis" and names no position or size, and the guide does not identify the strip as that filter.

lamps.note: Appendix E: a "Power LED" on the front of the chassis (green solid on: system on and operating normally; green off: powered off; amber on: fault condition), and on each supply an OK lamp (green) and a FAILED lamp (amber), Tables 24 and 25. No port lamp, link lamp or fan lamp is described, so none is drawn; the chassis lamp's position is a guess at the lamp cluster in Figure 2.

lifecycle.note: SALE STATUS IS UNKNOWN. The guide, in 66 pages, says nothing about end-of-sale or end-of-life, and no other document for this model is held; a revision date is not a status. No end-of-sale date is written.

port-order.note: THE GUIDE PRINTS NO PORT NUMBER IN ANY FIGURE AND NONE IS RESOLVED IN THE ARTWORK, so no numeral is drawn. The ids port-1 to port-40 (SFP+) and port-41 to port-44 (QSFP28) follow the library's convention for stacked cages, down each column with the upper cage first. That order is a choice and not a reading. Interface names (the guide does not give them for the 5001) are not recorded.

ports.note: Chapter 1, Ports: "40 x One GE/10GE SFP+ ports", of which "16 x Regular 10G SFP+ Ports" and "24 x DWDM and ZR Capable 10G SFP+ Ports (Purple in color)", and "4 x 100G QSFP28 ports (Light Green in color)". WHICH 24 OF THE 40 ARE THE DWDM PORTS IS NOT STATED and is not drawn: all forty are one group. Features: "A management and console interface are on the port (front) side of the router whereas the USB interface on the fan (back) side". Appendix D: the console is "an asynchronous RS-232 serial port with an RJ-45 connector". The guide describes no timing port; none is modelled.

rear-face.note: Figure 1 (back, fan side), left to right as drawn: a power supply, two fan modules, a centre block, a power supply. The centre block holds a USB port stood on end and, to its left, two round features the guide does not name; they are drawn as two unnamed 8 mm discs at about 0.2 and 0.45 of the block from its fan-side edge, a third of a fan-module height across (see the gaps). Each fan module's handle is the loop the figure shows, not a bar (the fan module's own provenance has the figure and size). Module widths are fractions of the face width along its near edge: a supply reads about a quarter, a fan about a fifth, the centre block a tenth. Slot height is the one-rack-unit face less a little clearance.

sources.note: One document: Hardware Installation Guide for Cisco NCS 5000 Series Routers, first published 2015-12-23, last modified 2019-01-31 (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/iosxr/ncs5000/hardware-install/b-ncs5000-hardware-installation-guide.pdf). It is an old revision and a newer one may exist. HELD AND SEARCHED FOR THIS MODEL: the guide's text and figures, and the intake notes for the NCS line. NOT HELD: a data sheet, a NetBox device type or elevation, a photograph, a 3D model. THE GUIDE'S FACE FIGURES (1 and 2) ARE GREYSCALE THREE-QUARTER VIEWS at 1029 x 167 and 781 x 481 px; there is no flat front or rear panel figure, so every position below is read off a perspective drawing.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180), by the rule and not by observation: Figure 2's resolution does not show which way the cages' lips face.

weight.note: THE GUIDE GIVES TWO FIGURES. Table 11: "Cisco NCS 5001 with two 650W power supplies, and two fan modules, 21 lb (9.5 kg)". The chassis-weight guidance in Chapter 2 says the router "with two power supplies, weighs 22 lb". The table is carried (it names its configuration); both are a loaded weight, so no empty-chassis weight is written.
